reason: The warm surroundings appear to start the heat-loss sequence.
expectation: The body will respond to the warmth, setting up cooling through the skin.

effect: The warmth produced a sensed warming state, suggesting the next step is a cooling response.
reaction: The signals to the brain make the transition clear.
reason: Sweat glands are directly relevant to the goal of cooling through evaporation.
expectation: The warming signal will activate sweating.

effect: The warming response first widens skin vessels, bringing more blood near the surface; sweating appears to come later.
reaction: I was surprised the vessel response had to come before sweating.
reason: Sweat glands are the next visible component needed for evaporative cooling.
expectation: The warming response will activate sweat glands and wet the skin.

effect: The skin is now wet with sweat, and the result identifies evaporation as the next step for heat loss.
reaction: The distinction between sweating and evaporation makes the cooling process clearer.
reason: Air at the skin is the visible component associated with evaporation.
expectation: Sweat will evaporate and carry heat away from the body.

effect: Evaporation completed the cooling goal, and the new goal calls for a response to cold.
reaction: The fading sweat signal helps show how the response changes as temperature returns toward its earlier range.
reason: The cold evening is the visible trigger for the new goal.
expectation: The body will sense the cold and begin a heat-conserving response.

effect: The body has sensed the cold, and the reduced sweat signal suggests it is beginning to limit heat loss.
reaction: The separate sweat signal makes the change from the warm response clear.
reason: The skin vessels changed during the warm response, so they are a plausible next step for conserving heat in the cold.
expectation: The skin vessels will narrow, reducing blood flow near the surface and heat loss.

effect: Narrowed skin vessels reduce heat loss, but the result says a separate response is needed to make heat.
reaction: The distinction between conserving heat and making it is clear.
reason: Skeletal muscle is the remaining visible component that could generate heat.
expectation: The muscles will shiver and produce heat.

effect: Shivering completed the cold response: repeated muscle contractions use ATP and produce heat, complementing the reduced heat loss from narrowed skin vessels.
reaction: Connecting muscle work and ATP use to heat production was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Combining the cold response with skeletal muscle brought together heat conservation and heat production, connecting this chapter to the earlier muscle work.

leastWorthwhile.text: The required vessel response before sweating was initially unclear. The compatibility feedback resolved it, but the sequence felt prescribed.

surprise.text: I expected to activate sweating immediately, but the game first directed me to the skin vessels.

arbitrary.text: Requiring the vessel change before sweating felt somewhat arbitrary because the visible goal did not explain that ordering.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it offered a similarly clear connection between body systems, though I would hope for more meaningful choices than a largely prescribed sequence.
